claims.text: Partial annealing at 500–600 °C promotes short-range atomic ordering in as-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type alloys.
Moderate annealing reduces residual strain in the as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi-type alloy.
Short-range ordering and residual-strain reduction smooth the magnetostructural transition.
Smoothing the magnetostructural transition diminishes hysteresis losses.
Partial annealing can reduce hysteresis without significantly degrading the magnetocaloric response.
The as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi thin films or ribbons have a predominantly hexagonal magnetostructural phase.
The as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi thin films or ribbons contain residual stresses.
Annealing temperature and dwell time can be used to control ordering and phase stability in high-entropy alloys.
The proposed 500–600 °C annealing window can induce ordering while minimizing unwanted secondary-phase formation in FeMnNiGeSi-type alloys.
Defect relaxation and localized ordering occur within the hexagonal matrix during partial annealing.
Heat treatment can make a high-entropy alloy magnetically more homogeneous.
More uniform short-range atomic ordering mitigates the discontinuous transformations responsible for large hysteresis during low-field cycling.
Increasing annealing exposure within the proposed window progressively reduces hysteresis-loop width.
Reduced hysteresis-loop width lowers associated energy loss.
The peak magnetocaloric effect changes only modestly after partial annealing.
The as-deposited baseline has a large, sharp magnetostructural transition with significant hysteresis.
The beneficial annealing effect holds above 500 °C and below the onset of extensive grain growth or second-phase formation.
Excessive annealing temperature or dwell time can cause secondary phases or compositional segregation that degrade magnetocaloric properties.
